prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a chosen protein to the ubiquitin-proteasome system and cause its destruction, through bifunctional degraders and molecular glues

statement.case_for: Round 1 did not change my view of the science. Targeted protein degradation turns ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical event: a small molecule forms a ternary complex that brings a target to an E3 ligase, and the cell does the rest. The ternary-complex structures, cooperativity measurements and degradation kinetics are the quantitative, independently reproduced evidence I look for, and the principle works across target classes and across two ligases (cereblon and VHL). The chair's summary shows B045 is the only ballot with three explicit supporters, all naming the same trio, and six of eight members place it in a first choice or alternative. I do not treat that count as evidence. My reason for staying is that no other shortlisted achievement combines a measured mechanism, generality and a new capability. The molecular-glue branch is clinically mature already, which answers part of the timing objection, and the PROTAC branch has the concept and first proofs in the Crews and Deshaies work.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is an approved drug, so the clinical verdict on the bifunctional branch is still open, and a prize now would honour a mechanism and a concept ahead of outcome. Credit is also genuinely crowded: Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim (first proof of concept) and Ito (cereblon with Handa) all fall outside a three-name cut. The PROTAC and glue strands were found by different people in different ways, so the citation has to say honestly that it rewards the principle and the cereblon mechanism, not the later optimisation. If the committee insists on clinical approval first, B069 is the better prize this year.

responses.point: Daniel asks that the citation state openly that it rewards the concept and the cereblon mechanism and not the optimisation work by Ciulli and Gray, and says he is more worried than I am about timing.
responses.response: I accept the wording point and have adopted it: my citation names the principle of redirecting the ubiquitin-proteasome system and lists the two routes, bifunctional degraders and molecular glues, so it does not claim the VHL optimisation or clinical candidates. On timing I move a little towards you. The glue branch you point out is already in approved drugs and its mechanism is measured at atomic resolution, so the maturity objection falls mainly on the PROTAC strand. I would not wait for an approved PROTAC, but I agree we should say clearly that the case is mechanistic and conceptual.

responses.point: Heiner supports the same trio, and his first alternative is B069. He asks whether the citation should state the principle of degradation and not one compound class, and presses on the discovered, not designed, nature of cereblon glues.
responses.response: I agree with the principle-level citation, and that is why I keep Handa and not a PROTAC-only pair: the cereblon mechanism turned a decades-old drug puzzle into a ligase-recruitment chemistry that is the same induced-proximity logic in another form. On the chair's question about Ciulli, I would still not displace Handa. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures refined and extended a principle whose proof was already in place, whereas cereblon opened a second, independent route. I accept that Ciulli is a close fourth and I would not call the exclusion obvious.

responses.point: Peter prefers B069 for Buchwald and Hartwig, with the cleanest attribution, long confirmation and heavy use, and ranks degraders low because no PROTAC is approved and credit is split between strands.
responses.response: This is the strongest competing case, and I changed my alternatives because of it: B069 replaces B032 as my first alternative. The shift from tin amides to free amines and bulky phosphines, tested against isolated intermediates, is a real chemical addition to the 2010 area, and his point on the cut between strands applies to my trio. Where I still differ is on weighing. Clean credit and maturity matter, but they do not outweigh a new mode of action that already has approved drugs on the glue side. I would support B069 if the committee decides a mature method with clean attribution should come first.

responses.point: Xiaodong says the C-N coupling work rests on mechanistic evidence and not only on scope, that the ligand-design logic was tested against intermediates and kinetics, and that degraders are not yet ready because eight names are credited and general rules for productive degradation are unsettled.
responses.response: The mechanistic point on B069 is useful, and as someone who trusts measurement I give it weight. I partly agree on degraders: predictive rules for productive ternary complexes and degradation are incomplete, and I would not claim otherwise in a citation. But the same is true of many recognised discoveries, and incomplete prediction does not make the mechanism doubtful. The eight-name list is a reason to write the citation narrowly and to keep to the strands whose mechanism is reproduced, not a reason to defer.

responses.point: Johan prefers B009 for Cullis, Anderson and Langer, argues that the pH-dependent ionizable lipid is a single design principle and that delivery completes the 2023 Medicine story, and rates attribution as his weak point.
responses.response: His pKa-design argument moved me: I now accept that there is a real molecular principle there, not just formulation, and I withdraw the word optimisation as a complete description. My remaining difficulty is the one he concedes himself. The Vancouver and MIT strands, with Hope, Madden and MacLachlan, cannot be cut to three names without a priority argument I find harder than the Handa-versus-Ciulli question. I keep B009 out of my alternatives for that reason, though I would take the Cullis-centred framing seriously if the committee can settle attribution.

uncertainties: Whether the citation should cover both the bifunctional and molecular-glue strands or only one
Whether recognition should wait for an approved PROTAC, given that the glue branch is already clinical
Whether Handa or Ciulli (or Ito) belongs in the third place of the trio
Whether the committee will weigh a clean-credit mature method (B069) above a new modality
Relative standing of base editing (B026) after the 2020 CRISPR prize if B045 is judged early
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal need arises from my profile. I have no personal, institutional or collaborative link to any credited name on the shortlist. My field, nucleotide metabolism and DNA replication fidelity, is topically adjacent to B026 and B050, but that is topical interest only. No disclosure has changed since round 1.
